report.tagline: A UK online used car seller that grew to an $8 billion valuation, collapsed in 2024, and now lives on as a car listings site owned by Motors.
report.simpleSummary: Cazoo let you buy a used car on your phone, like ordering from Amazon. It owned the cars, cleaned and checked them, and delivered them to your door in about 72 hours, with 7 days to return it for a full refund. It spent huge sums on football shirts and TV ads to become famous fast. It lost far more money on each car than it could ever make back, went into administration in May 2024, and the name was sold to Motors, which relaunched it in 2025 as a site that lists other dealers' cars.

overview.whatItDoes: From 2019 to 2024 Cazoo bought used cars, reconditioned them in its own centres, and sold them online with home delivery or collection from a Cazoo hub. Buyers paid in full or took finance, and could part-exchange their old car. Since April 2025 the Cazoo brand is a listings marketplace run by Motors.co.uk, where independent and franchise dealers advertise cars and Cazoo does not own the stock.
howItWorks: Old model: Cazoo bought cars from auctions, leasing firms and the public, so it carried every car on its own balance sheet.
Each car got a 300-point check, cleaning and repairs in a Cazoo reconditioning centre before being photographed for the site.
Buyers chose a car online, paid or arranged finance, and had it delivered in about 72 hours.
A 7-day money-back guarantee and a 90-day warranty were meant to replace the trust of seeing the car first.
New model (2025): dealers pay Motors to list cars on Cazoo, buyers search and then contact or visit the dealer.
overview.valueProposition: Old model: buy a checked used car without haggling or visiting a forecourt, with a free return if you do not like it. New model: one place to search a large share of UK used cars from trusted dealers.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Complete purchase in the app or site and get the car delivered in about 72 hours.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: The core promise that set Cazoo apart from dealers, and also its most expensive operation.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Return the car within 7 days for a full refund, with free collection.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Built trust for a big purchase made without a test drive. Every return cost Cazoo transport and reconditioning money.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Cazoo inspected and repaired each car in its own centres before sale.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Meant to guarantee quality. When it failed, as BBC Watchdog showed in 2022, trust broke quickly.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Online finance applications and instant valuations of the buyer's old car.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Finance commissions added profit per car and made monthly payments easier for buyers.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Monthly car subscription including insurance and servicing, launched after buying Drover in 2021.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Aimed at repeat monthly revenue, but tied up even more money in cars.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Dealers list stock on Cazoo through Motors; buyers search and contact dealers.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Asset-light model: no cars owned, revenue from dealer subscriptions instead.

steps.detail: Notices Cazoo on a football shirt or TV ad.
Filters by budget, body type and mileage on the site.
Looks at 360-degree photos and the list of marked imperfections.
Pays a deposit or applies for finance online, adds part-exchange.
Picks a delivery slot about 72 hours out.
Driver hands over the car and collects any part-exchange.
Has 7 days to return it for a full refund.
Finds a warning light or damage not shown online.
Calls or emails customer service, often with long waits.
Cazoo books a truck to collect the car.
Refund and finance cancellation are processed.
Posts on Trustpilot or social media, which shapes others' trust.

userJourneys.name: Dealer lists stock on new Cazoo

steps.detail: Joins via Motors, often bundled with an existing Motors package.
Cars flow in automatically from the dealer's stock system.
Buyers send enquiries or call from Cazoo listings.
Checks cost per lead against Auto Trader.
Stays only if Cazoo leads turn into sales.

businessModel.summary: Old Cazoo made money on the gap between what it paid for a car and what it sold it for, plus finance commission and add-ons. That gap was too small to cover reconditioning, delivery, returns and massive marketing. New Cazoo makes money from monthly fees dealers pay to list cars.

revenueStreams.detail: Retail price of each car; most of revenue but thin margin.
Lenders paid Cazoo a cut for each finance deal arranged.
Extended warranty, GAP insurance and paint protection.
Monthly fees for car subscriptions, closed down before the collapse.
Dealers pay Motors a monthly package to appear on Cazoo.

businessModel.pricing: Old model: fixed car prices, typically £10,000 to £25,000, delivery sometimes charged. New model: dealer listing packages, not public.
costDrivers: Buying stock and holding about 1,500+ cars at any time
Reconditioning centres and a 55-acre Midlands site
Delivery trucks and drivers, plus collecting returns
Sponsorships across Premier League football, rugby, cricket, golf and snooker
22 showrooms and hubs, and a European expansion that was shut in 2022
businessModel.unitEconomics: Rough walk-through, estimated: Cazoo sells a car for £15,000 that it bought for about £13,800. That leaves about £1,200 of gross profit, the money left after the car's own cost. Add finance commission and add-ons for maybe £500 more, so about £1,700. Then reconditioning costs about £600, delivery and any return about £300, and marketing to win that buyer often £1,000 or more. Before paying for offices, tech and staff, each car already loses hundreds of pounds. A £704 million loss in 2022 on roughly 60,000 to 70,000 cars works out to a loss of around £10,000 per car once everything is counted. Selling more cars made the hole bigger, not smaller.

howTheyGetUsers: Huge sponsorships: shirts for Everton, Aston Villa and others, plus the World Snooker Championship and The Hundred
Buying other companies such as Drover, Smart Fleet Solutions and Cluno for faster expansion
2025 model: traffic from Motors.co.uk and leftover brand fame
whatBringsUsersBack: Car buying is rare, about once every 3 to 4 years, so repeat purchase was weak
Selling the car back to Cazoo at the next upgrade
Subscription was meant to create monthly repeat customers
growth.moat: Cazoo had almost no moat. Brand fame was bought with ads, not earned through habit. Anyone with money could copy the online buying flow, and big dealers like Arnold Clark and Motorpoint already had cheaper stock and local sites. The relaunched marketplace has a better chance because listing networks gain value as more dealers and buyers join, but Auto Trader is far ahead.

competitors.name: Auto Trader
competitors.positioning: The UK's biggest car listings site, highly profitable from dealer fees.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: New Cazoo pitches itself as a cheaper Auto Trader challenger, but has far fewer buyers today.

competitors.name: Cinch
competitors.positioning: Online used car retailer owned by Constellation Automotive (BCA, webuyanycar).
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Cinch had cheap supply from its parent's auctions; Cazoo had to buy stock at market price.

competitors.name: Motorpoint
competitors.positioning: Profitable listed used car retailer with large physical sites plus online sales.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Motorpoint grew slowly and kept costs low; Cazoo spent to grow first.

competitors.name: Carvana (US) and Spinny (India)
competitors.positioning: Online used car retailers in other markets with the same own-the-car model.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Carvana nearly failed in 2022 but survived by cutting costs; Spinny raised money more slowly and focused on a few cities and repeat buyers. Cazoo expanded to 5 countries before the UK model worked.

northStar.metric: Cars delivered and kept past the 7-day return window, per month
northStar.why: This is the north star because a car that is kept means the buyer got what they paid for. It also only counts sales that make money, because returned cars cost Cazoo twice.

guardrailMetrics: Days a car sits in stock before sale
strengths: Very strong brand awareness built in about two years
Simple, well-designed online buying flow that buyers liked when it worked
Clear trust promises: 7-day returns and a warranty
The brand was valuable enough that Motors paid up to £5 million for it
weaknesses: Lost money on every car, so growth made losses bigger
Owned all stock, so it needed huge amounts of cash
Expanded into France, Germany, Italy and Spain before the UK was profitable
Quality control failed at scale, as BBC Watchdog showed in April 2022
Spent heavily on sponsorships that bought awareness, not loyalty
risks: Rising interest rates in 2022 made stock and finance more expensive and ended cheap investor money
Used car prices swung sharply after the pandemic, hurting the value of stock it held
Strong rivals with cheaper supply, such as Cinch and Motorpoint
For new Cazoo: Auto Trader's grip on UK dealers and buyers
userComplaints: Cars delivered with faults, damage or missing items
Delivery dates missed or changed at the last minute
Hard to reach customer service and slow refunds
After the collapse, confusion about warranties on cars already bought
In 2025, some buyers do not realise Cazoo now only lists dealer cars

improvementIdeas.idea: Grow in one country and a few regions only until each car makes money
improvementIdeas.problem: Expansion to five countries burned cash before the model worked anywhere.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Smaller losses and time to fix operations.

improvementIdeas.idea: Swap national sponsorships for search and referral marketing
improvementIdeas.problem: Sponsorships created fame but a very high cost per sale.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Lower marketing cost per car sold.

improvementIdeas.idea: Video condition report for every car before payment
improvementIdeas.problem: Buyers received cars that did not match the photos, driving returns.

improvementIdeas.idea: Let partner dealers sell through Cazoo instead of owning every car
improvementIdeas.problem: Owning all stock tied up cash and made price swings dangerous.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More choice without stock risk, which is the path Motors took in 2025.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of sales from partner stock

improvementIdeas.idea: New Cazoo: show a clear 'how this works' banner and dealer ratings
improvementIdeas.problem: Buyers still expect Cazoo to sell and deliver cars itself.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer confused leads and better dealer satisfaction.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Lead to sale rate reported by dealers

pmLessons: Fix unit economics first. If each car loses money, selling more cars only makes the loss grow faster.
Paid fame is not product-market fit. Cazoo was famous, but buyers came once every few years and did not come back.
Trust promises need operations to back them. A 7-day return policy is only as good as the cars and support behind it.
Cheap money hides bad models. When interest rates rose in 2022, the plan to raise more funding stopped working.
A failed company's brand can still have value if it is moved to a cheaper model, like a marketplace.

interviewQuestions.question: Why did Cazoo fail when Spinny in India is still running?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare unit economics, speed of expansion, marketing spend, and funding climate. Point out that Spinny focused on fewer cities and assured quality, while Cazoo went into five countries at once.

interviewQuestions.question: You are the PM at Cazoo in 2021. What one metric would you watch, and why?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick profit per car or kept rate after 7 days, explain why revenue or units alone mislead, and name the levers under it.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce returns in an online used car business?
interviewQuestions.hint: Map the reasons for return (condition, fit, price regret), then propose better photos or video, honest damage reports, and test drive options. Track return rate and cost per return.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Motors keep the Cazoo brand as a marketplace or merge it into Motors?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh brand awareness against confusion and past bad press. Look at buyer traffic, dealer leads and cost per lead versus Auto Trader.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a trust feature for buying a car you have never seen in person.
interviewQuestions.hint: Start with the buyer's fear, then list options (inspection video, third-party check, return window, warranty). Pick one, define success and the cost risk.

glossary.meaning: A shell company that lists on a stock exchange and then merges with a private firm, letting it go public faster than a normal listing.
A UK legal process where outside administrators take over a failing company to sell what they can and repay lenders.
How much money a business makes or loses on one item sold or one customer.
The money left from a sale after paying for the item itself, before other costs like staff and ads.
A business that connects buyers and sellers and takes a fee, without owning the goods itself.
When a product meets a real need so well that customers keep coming back and tell others.
Something that makes it hard for competitors to copy a business or steal its customers.
The one metric a team treats as the best sign that customers are getting value.
How many months a company can keep running on the cash it has before it needs more money.

assumptions: The per-car unit economics walk-through is an estimate built from reported total losses and typical UK used car margins, not from Cazoo's own per-car figures.
About 60,000 to 70,000 cars sold in 2022 is an estimate from memory of company results; check the 2022 annual report.
Typical car price of £10,000 to £25,000 is inferred from the type of stock Cazoo sold.
Current (2026) size of the relaunched marketplace was not found; the 2025 launch figures are used.
